description.plain_text: ModelBuilder Use the ModelBuilder to create a 3D model for a shot given a tracked camera. You can build a model by creating shapes then editing them; and you can align models over your shot footage by dragging vertices to their corresponding 2D location. Create: Use the left-hand toolbar to create a Point, Card, Cube, Sphere, Cone or Cylinder shape. You can set default values for creating new shapes such as distance and tessellation. When you create a new shape it will be added to the scene graph tree in the properties panel. You can use the scene-graph to name, order, group and set the visibility for shapes. Create a new group using the '+' button, then drag and drop to create a hierarchy. Align: Align mode calculates a 3D position for an object that matches its position in the source footage as closely as possible without distorting the shape. To use it you must have an input camera and the viewer must be locked to it; this will happen automatically whenever you switch into Align mode. Position shapes by dragging several of their vertices over their correct 2D locations; then change to a different frame and repeat the process. It should only be necessary to do this for 4 or 5 of the vertices for each object. When you've placed a vertex on one frame, a guideline will be shown on other frames to indicate where the correct location might be. Edit: Starting with one of the primitive shapes, you can perform various editing operations to sculpt it into the shape you desire. Editing operations include moving, scaling, carving, extruding and bevelling. Operations apply to the currently selected vertices, edges, faces or shapes and are found on the viewer's right-click menu. Press Enter to accept the results of an operation or Escape to cancel it. Tips: You can use input geometry as a reference while modelling. Select vertices on the input geo before creating a shape and the created shape will be fitted to the vertices automatically. The PointCloudGenerator is especially handy for this. You can hold down Shift to place a new shape on the surface of some existing geometry. If you keep Shift held down while you move the cursor, the yellow circle will change orientation to match the geometry underneath the cursor. Carving has to start on an existing edge or vertex; subsequent clicks must be inside the highlighted area. You can do freehand carving by holding down Ctrl+Shift while you drag the mouse.
description.text:
ModelBuilder

Use the ModelBuilder to create a 3D model for a shot given a tracked camera. You can build a model by creating shapes then editing them; and you can align models over your shot footage by dragging vertices to their corresponding 2D location.

Create:

Use the left-hand toolbar to create a Point, Card, Cube, Sphere, Cone or Cylinder shape. You can set default values for creating new shapes such as distance and tessellation. When you create a new shape it will be added to the scene graph tree in the properties panel. You can use the scene-graph to name, order, group and set the visibility for shapes. Create a new group using the '+' button, then drag and drop to create a hierarchy.

Align:

Align mode calculates a 3D position for an object that matches its position in the source footage as closely as possible without distorting the shape. To use it you must have an input camera and the viewer must be locked to it; this will happen automatically whenever you switch into Align mode. Position shapes by dragging several of their vertices over their correct 2D locations; then change to a different frame and repeat the process. It should only be necessary to do this for 4 or 5 of the vertices for each object. When you've placed a vertex on one frame, a guideline will be shown on other frames to indicate where the correct location might be.

Edit:

Starting with one of the primitive shapes, you can perform various editing operations to sculpt it into the shape you desire. Editing operations include moving, scaling, carving, extruding and bevelling. Operations apply to the currently selected vertices, edges, faces or shapes and are found on the viewer's right-click menu. Press Enter to accept the results of an operation or Escape to cancel it.

Tips:
  • You can use input geometry as a reference while modelling. Select vertices on the input geo before creating a shape and the created shape will be fitted to the vertices automatically. The PointCloudGenerator is especially handy for this.
  • You can hold down Shift to place a new shape on the surface of some existing geometry. If you keep Shift held down while you move the cursor, the yellow circle will change orientation to match the geometry underneath the cursor.
  • Carving has to start on an existing edge or vertex; subsequent clicks must be inside the highlighted area. You can do freehand carving by holding down Ctrl+Shift while you drag the mouse.
